title: Refactor the card into an architecture
prompt:
Refactor this slice of the old stylesheet. Keep the HTML as it is.

1. Declare layers including **`reset`, `tokens`, `components`, `utilities`** in that order (you may add `layouts` or others in between), and put every rule in a layer.
2. No ID selectors and no `!important` anywhere.
3. The card's accent border reads a **`--card-accent`** token that defaults to `#6d28d9`; `.theme-sponsor` sets it to **`#0e7490`**.
4. `.u-hidden` still hides the Draft badge.
5. Cards have **no margins of their own**; the `.schedule` layout puts **16px** between them.
hints: Start with the layer statement, then move each existing rule into the layer that matches its job.
Tokens: `:root { --card-accent: #6d28d9; }` and `.theme-sponsor { --card-accent: #0e7490; }`. The card uses `border-inline-start: 6px solid var(--card-accent);`.
Spacing: delete the card's margin and give `.schedule` `display: grid; gap: 16px;`. Put `.u-hidden` in the utilities layer, without `!important`.
explanation: The layer statement moves conflict resolution out of selectors: `.u-hidden` in the last layer beats the component's `display: inline-block` with plain (0,1,0) specificity, so neither IDs nor `!important` are needed. The card reads `--card-accent` instead of a hard-coded color, so `.theme-sponsor` re-themes every card inside it with one custom property, and any future part of the card that uses the accent follows automatically. Moving spacing to `.schedule { gap: 16px; }` lets the same card drop into a sidebar or carousel without fighting a built-in margin.

checks.layer-order: Layers reset, tokens, components, utilities are declared in order
checks.accent-token: Regular cards use the violet --card-accent token
checks.sponsor-theme: Sponsor cards are teal through the token
checks.utility-wins: The u-hidden utility still hides the Draft badge
checks.layout-owns-spacing: Cards have no margins; the layout spaces them 16px apart
